summary: UPDATE changes values in rows that already exist, and DELETE removes rows. Both use WHERE to pick which rows.
notes: UPDATE and DELETE print nothing in the sqlite3 shell. Run a SELECT to check the result.
The WHERE uses both student_id and course_id so only one enrollment changes, not all of Ethan's classes.
A WHERE that matches no rows is not an error. Nothing changes and nothing is printed.
pitfall: Forgetting WHERE changes every row: DELETE FROM enrollments; empties the whole table, and UPDATE enrollments SET grade = 85; gives every student an 85. Run the WHERE as a SELECT first.
